title: Warmstart playlist: 90-minute SDK interop & telemetry run
content:
Goal:
A compact, prescriptive "warmstart" playlist engineers can complete in ~90 minutes to go from repo -> instrumented sample app -> smoke tests. Focus: interop with Redwood hosted API, basic telemetry (latency/cost tokens), and safe fallback hooks.

Audience:
- Product engineers shipping first Redwood integration
- Solutions engineers running a customer demo
- Internal dev advocates/bootcamp leaders

Constraints / design decisions (why this exists):
- 90 minutes fits a half-day workshop slot or a quick pairing session
- Telemetry first: team should leave with an initial signal for cost/latency tradeoffs
- Minimal infra: local dev + Redwood free credits / sandbox token only
- Interop-focused: exercise SDK calls + fallback to curl / HTTP for compatibility checks

High-level flow (timeboxed):
0–10m: prep + expectations
- Install Node 18+ / Python 3.10 (note exact versions in quick-links below)
- Clone starter repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter (branch: warmstart)
- Get sandbox API key + free credits (link in onboarding email)

10–30m: basic hello world + run with Redwood SDK
- Task: run sample that calls Redwood text generation and embeddings
- Commands (node):
  - npm ci
  - cp .env.example .env && edit REDWOOD_API_KEY
  - npm run start:sample -> confirm generation appears in terminal
- Acceptance: successful 1-shot completion and visible request id in logs

30–50m: add simple fallback (HTTP + short-circuit)
- Motivation: show how to fallback to an alternate model variant or local stub when latency > 500ms
- Implementation notes: lightweight wrapper that measures client-side RTT, if >500ms then call local stub server (included in repo)
- Smoke test: flip a feature flag (env var) to force fallback and confirm behavior

50–75m: instrument minimal telemetry (token counts, latency, error rates)
- Objective: produce a single JSON line per request written to stdout that contains: request_id, tokens_out, tokens_in, model, latency_ms, route_taken (hosted|fallback)
- Implementation hints: SDK exposes token counters on response.metadata.tokens; if not present, compute from response.text length as fallback heuristic
- Where to store: local file logs/warmstart-events.log for workshop; show how to upload to internal observability later
- Quick visualization: run jq to aggregate 10 requests and show avg latency / cost estimate

75–85m: run a mini-regression harness (prompt bank)
- Use prompts/prompts-warmstart.json (5 short prompts) and run them in parallel to observe distribution
- Expected output: at least one outlier >1s latency, one request hitting fallback if you set small concurrency limits

85–90m: wrap-up checklist + next steps
- Save a copy of logs and attach to ticket DEVEX-234 for analysis
- Open a short retro doc: what was confusing? where did SDK ergonomics break down?
- Optional: schedule 1:1 sandbox review with SEs if customer demo is planned

Files in the starter repo (what participants will touch):
- README.md (quickstart + trouble common issues section)
- examples/sample-app (node + python examples)
- examples/local-stub (tiny HTTP stub for fallback)
- scripts/telemetry-shipper.sh (simple uploader to S3 dev bucket - opt-in)
- prompts/prompts-warmstart.json (small curated prompt set)
- smoke/ci-smoke.js (single-file runner used in workshop)

Developer notes / gotchas (trimmed list):
- API key boundary: make clear that sandbox keys auto-expire in 7 days; warn about hardcoding keys in examples
- Token accounting: open models report tokens differently; treat reported token counts as guidance, not billing truth
- CORS pitfalls: browser demos require proxy or server-side relay; avoid teaching browser direct calls during the 90m flow
- Local stub: include deterministic responses to avoid flakiness in demos

Pedagogy & delivery tips for workshop leads:
- Run one live request slowly (share terminal) to show internal state (request id, headers, token metadata)
- Pair participants by role: one edits prompts, one watches telemetry to encourage cross-functional learning
- Use feature toggles (env vars) to demonstrate safe rollback; show how a single flag flips to fallback route
- If time, demo Rollouts feature in Console: show how to pin model versions for canary vs default

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Should the telemetry snippet ship as a tiny npm package (warmstart-telemetry) or remain as copy/paste in examples? (decision required by 2026-03-01)
- Do we include a short section on cost estimation per prompt? prototype formula in DEVEX-234 but need review from Pricing team
- Add a tiny browser proxy example? (pros: easier demos, cons: more setup for attendees)

Links & quick refs for participants:
- Branch (warmstart): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter/tree/warmstart
- Minimal API quick reference (internal): confluence:DEVEX/Warmstart-API-snippets
- Known tickets: DEVEX-234 (telemetry pkg), SDK-451 (fallback wrapper API parity)
- Slack threads: #devex-warmstart (pin: starter checklist message)

Appendix: short checklist artifact for participants to paste into a ticket after workshop:
- repo + branch used
- environment (node/python versions)
- sample logs attached (logs/warmstart-events.log)
- any failing prompts or unexpected outputs (copy/paste)
- screenshot of Console model route if used

Rough timeline for shipping this doc and examples to master:
- Draft + starter repo updates: 2 weeks (Ava + Rahul)
- UX pass + README polish: 1 week (Maya)
- Small beta with 3 SEs (run 3 workshops): 1 week
- Gather feedback and finalize: 1 week

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep the playbook intentionally opinionated: pick defaults that are safe and easy to explain (short seq length, default batching off, small model by default)
- Remove heavyweight observability (Datadog/OTel) from default path; optional appendix for power users
- Make fallback wrapper tiny and copy/paste friendly; put more advanced config behind a single toggle

-- end --
